results.label: Custom domain uses a GA feature
results.why: Cloud Run domain mappings are Preview and Google says not to use pre-GA offerings with PHI; the load balancer path is GA.
results.detail: global external Application Load Balancer with a Google-managed certificate

results.label: Cloud SQL has no public IP
results.why: With --no-assign-ip the database is reachable only inside the VPC.

results.label: Database connections must use TLS
results.why: ENCRYPTED_ONLY refuses unencrypted connections, even inside the VPC.

results.label: Point-in-time recovery on
results.why: Daily backups alone lose up to a day; PITR restores to a moment within the log retention window.

results.label: Deletion protection on
results.why: A mistyped delete command cannot remove the instance.

results.label: Secret pinned to a version
results.why: Environment-variable secrets are read when an instance starts, so "latest" lets instances of one revision hold different passwords after a rotation.

results.label: App runs as its own service account
results.why: The default compute service account often holds the project-wide Editor role.
results.detail: dedicated account, two secrets and one bucket

results.label: Runtime account has no project-wide roles
results.why: Access is granted on the secret and the bucket, so a compromised instance cannot reach anything else.

results.label: run.app address closed once the domain is live
results.why: With the load balancer in front, ingress "internal and Cloud Load Balancing" blocks direct requests to the run.app URL.

results.label: Nothing public before smoke tests
results.why: The first deploy requires an identity token; the public binding comes after the load balancer and TLS.

results.label: Startup probe checks the database
results.why: Cloud Run waits for the startup probe before a deployment succeeds, so a revision that cannot log in never takes traffic.

results.label: Bucket locked down
results.why: Uniform bucket-level access and public access prevention stop object ACLs and public links.

results.label: Password can rotate without dropping requests
results.why: PostgreSQL holds one password per login; two logins let the new revision start on fresh credentials before the old ones are retired.

results.label: My access expires by itself
results.why: Every grant to my account carries an IAM condition with an end date.

results.label: Everything in one region
results.why: Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, the connector, the bucket and the secrets sit together; the serverless NEG must be in the service's region.
